Close attempt (sanctioned non-force path) — STILL OPEN.

1) 'rebar transition 39c5-d81a-aad6-4e21 open closed' failed with:
   plan-review close gate: unsigned: no certified plan-review attestation. Run rebar review-plan 39c5-d81a-aad6-4e21 separately, then retry close.

2) Ran the legitimate remedy 'rebar review-plan 39c5-d81a-aad6-4e21' (no --force). Verdict: BLOCK (exit 1), ONE blocking finding, signature {signed: false, reason: BLOCK}. Criteria F1/E6/E2: 'The benchmark acceptance criterion targets a fraction of the per-event wall-clock with no quantified threshold, making it unmeasurable and requiring executor judgment on what counts as pass.'

That is the SAME defect I flagged in the preceding comment and is why I left AC4 and AC5 unticked — the gate and I agree independently. The five implementation ACs are verified, ticked, and green; the two benchmark ACs are unverifiable as written.

Unlocking a close without a bypass needs one operator decision: replace 'a fraction of the per-event wall-clock' with a quantified, machine-checkable threshold (the shipped proxy is a >=10x COMMIT-count reduction, pinned by test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass), then re-run review-plan. No --force / --force-close was used.
